    Melee Duplicate

    At exactly 100% Crit Chance, every hit is a yellow crit that triggers Melee Duplicate. Going above 100% turns some yellows into harder-hitting orange crits that do not trigger a duplicate.

    However, stronger orange crits—including on duplicate hits—can outweigh the missed procs. Find the Crit Chance that gives the highest average damage for your Critical Multiplier.

    Relic Staggering vs. Radshare

    Fair comparison: each squad member owns ONE copy of the same target relic. The squad uses exactly the same number of target relics in both strategies. Staggering requires extra filler relics.

    ⚡

    All at once · Radshare

    Everyone cracks the same target relic together every round. Best when you want the drop as fast as possible, but simultaneous target drops are wasted because each player can pick only one reward per mission.

    One at a time · Stagger

    Only one player uses the target relic each round, while everyone else brings filler ("trash") relics. This maximizes potential copies from scarce target relics: with {s} players, staggering can yield up to {s} target copies per player instead of just one when opened all at once. Best for maximizing potential profit from those relics, at the cost of up to {s}× as many missions and extra filler relics.

    Riven Stat Range Calculator

    Pick the weapon type, riven layout and stats to see the exact roll range for each stat.

    Weapon type
    Riven layout
    Stats on the riven

    Spliced stat combinations

    A Riven Splicer consumes two matching stats on one riven and replaces them with the spliced stat plus one random stat. Only one spliced stat can be on a riven. Where a stat lists more than one recipe, either pair works.

    Base stat values

    Switch between positive and negative ranges, then pick a weapon category to see its base values and roll ranges for every riven layout.

    The whole formula

    Final value = base value × layout multiplier × roll

    Every riven stat is these three numbers multiplied together. Only the roll is random.

    Step 1: Base value

    Each stat has a base value that depends on the weapon category. Rifle damage is 198%, rifle critical chance is about 180%, and so on. Shotguns, pistols, archguns and melee weapons each have their own base values, and some stats only exist on certain categories. The full list is in the Show Base Stat Values table.

    Step 2: Layout multiplier

    How many positive and negative stats the riven has changes how strong each stat is. The multiplier is the same for every positive stat on the riven, and the negative stat has its own value.

    LayoutPositiveNegativeWhat it means
    2 pos, 0 neg0.99noneEach stat is at 99% of base value
    2 pos, 1 neg1.2375-0.495Each stat is boosted to 123.75% of base value
    3 pos, 0 neg0.75noneEach stat is 75% of base value
    3 pos, 1 neg0.9375-0.75Each stat is at 93.75% of base value

    Adding a negative boosts every positive by 25% compared to the same riven without one: 0.99 × 1.25 = 1.2375 and 0.75 × 1.25 = 0.9375.

    Step 3: The random roll

    Each stat rolls between 90% and 110% of its value, independently. That is where the min and max you see in the calculator come from: multiply by 0.9 for the lowest roll and by 1.1 for the highest.

    Putting it together

    Take the stat's base value for your weapon category, multiply by the layout multiplier to get the center value, then apply the 0.9 to 1.1 roll for the low and high ends.

    Worked example

    A rifle riven with 3 positive and 1 negative stat.

    Positive: damage (198% base)

    198 × 0.9375 = 185.6% center
    Low roll: 185.6 × 0.9 = 167.1%
    High roll: 185.6 × 1.1 = 204.2%

    Negative: a stat with a 108% base

    108 × -0.75 = -81% center
    Low roll: -81 × 0.9 = -72.9%
    High roll: -81 × 1.1 = -89.1%

    The negative uses its own value from the layout table, which is why it has a separate multiplier from the positives.
